title: The Glow-worm's Gentle Light
markdown:
Once, in the Moonlit Glade of the Whispering Woods, Alfie the hamster puffed his chest like a tiny drum. “I am the quickest,” he said. “I am the cleverest. I can find anything faster than anyone.” His boasts bounced off the old oaks and scattered slow ladybugs.

Moonpetal the unicorn grazed nearby. Her coat was as soft as moonlight, her silver mane a quiet waterfall. She listened more than she spoke, preferring the wind and the crickets to a contest of boasts. When she did speak, her voice was as soft as falling petals. She watched Alfie scurry, and she did not argue. Speed was his favourite story about himself.

Twilight painted the sky pink and purple. A playful wind tumbled through the glade, a chuckle in its howl, and the fireflies — the glade’s own lanterns — blinked out one by one. Familiar shapes melted. Field mice shivered. A baby owl blinked from its nest. “Oh dear,” whispered a rabbit. “How will we see?”

Alfie dashed at once. “Do not worry. I will fix this. I am the fastest.” Because he ran without looking, he bumped a sleepy badger. “Oof. Watch it, little fuzzball,” said the badger. Alfie tripped over a twisting root. He was so busy being the rescuer that he was not really helping. The night felt more uncertain, not less.

Moonpetal stood still. Unicorns see more than most, especially in quiet times. She remembered a softer lantern than fireflies. “Patience now,” she said. “There is another light. A quieter light.”

She trotted to the ferns, where glow-worms pulsed green on the moss, like little jewels. She nudged one gently with her nose. It crawled, a tiny beacon. Then another, and another. A trail of steady green wound back into the glade.

Alfie, who had stopped bumping into things, blinked. His boasts sat down beside him. “What is that?” he whispered.

The glow-worms lit the path for the mice, showed the baby owl its branch, and helped the rabbit find its mama. The forest seemed to sigh. Because Moonpetal had looked instead of rushed, the glade wore a sprinkle of tiny emeralds.

Alfie scampered to her, whiskers drooping. “I thought being fast and loud was the best way to help. You just saw things.”

Moonpetal nuzzled him. Her breath smelled of sweet clover. “Sometimes the quietest heart and the clearest eyes can find the truest light.”

And so the creatures of the glade learned that the gentlest help, offered with a watchful eye, can shine the brightest.
